headline: Large User Grid Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Budget Creates New Electricity Consumption Tax for Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia's 2026 budget includes a new electricity consumption tax of $0.011 per kWh for data centers, effective July 1, 2026, while preserving their sales and use tax exemption. This tax aims to make the industry pay its fair share for energy use and infrastructure, with an annual revenue cap of $600 million.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for future water management policies.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be aggregated and available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency on water consumption, a top complaint against the data center industry.

headline: Data Center Siting & Noise
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more authority to regulate the siting of data centers and establish noise limits to address community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates.
news_headline: Virginia hits data centers with new energy tax, water and noise rules
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes provisions for the Department of Environmental Quality to set the state's first data center noise standard by 2029, with violations leading to fines starting in 2030. This addresses long-standing resident complaints about noise pollution from data centers.
